Definition: from G4134 and G5409; to carry out fully (in evidence), i.e. completely assure (or convince), entirely accomplish:--most surely believe, fully know (persuade), make full proof of.
BiblicalUsage: Plerophoreo means to carry out fully, to be fully persuaded, to complete. Abraham was fully persuaded God could perform what He promised, in Romans 4:21. Paul tells Timothy to make full proof of his ministry in 2 Timothy 4:5, and Luke writes of the things most surely believed among us in Luke 1:1. Epaphras prays the Colossians may stand perfect and complete in Colossians 4:12.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe full persuasion is the quiet strength of Abraham — God said it, God can do it, that settles it. That is the faith I want.
